newsitem.title: USA: American Air to add extra flight during BA strike.
newsitem.headline: American Air to add extra flight during BA strike.

text.p: American Airlines said Wednesday it will add one daily flight from New York's Kennedy Airport to London Heathrow to accommodate passengers and cargo stranded by the cabin crew strike at British Airways Plc.
American Airlines, BA's betrothed alliance partner, said it has received an influx of calls from cargo customers affected by the strike.
BA grounded half of its flights out of London and about 20 to 30 percent of its flights worldwide after the Transport and General Workers' Union went on strike Wednesday morning.

"We're adding one extra section so we can accommodate additional cargo and we're also offering BA customers alternative capacity whereever possible," said Laura Mayo, a spokesperson for American Airlines cargo services.
American, a unit of AMR Corp, said it will add one extra daily flight from Wednesday through Friday. American normally offers four daily flights from Kennedy to Heathrow.
Other U.S. airlines, such as Delta Air Lines Inc and UAL Corp's United Airlines, are accepting some BA passengers, but said there were few empty seats available during the peak summer season.
"We are accommodating some customers. But this is the very busy travel season internationally, there's a minimal amount of seats available," said Bill Berry, a Delta spokesman said.
Delta and United said they did not plan to add extra flights, since their fleet and crews were already being fully used.
